notes.text: 0 orders. Risk-on day in Europe with metals up on a US-China truce extension and crude down as the Iran risk premium comes out. Most moves are continuations already priced in by midday, with US CPI pending as a two-way risk for copper, gold and chips, so nothing offers a named catalyst with an expected move well above round-trip cost.

Day one of the European paper account, 9 November 2026. The trader made no trades. Equity stays at 1000 euros, all in cash. The day result is zero and the total result is zero. No orders were sent, so there were no fills, no costs and no rejections. Custody cost was zero. Reconcile is consistent and there are no warnings. What moved: crude fell about 3.6 percent after Trump ruled out new Iran strikes. Gold, copper and European indices rose on a US-China truce extension. US CPI is still pending.

1 orders. Risk-on morning: Trump calls the Iran war 'effectively over', crude falls again, European index futures and drivers point up and VIX drops 22%, with US CPI later today as the main event risk. The only fresh, name-specific, low-cost catalyst is Infineon's record Q4 and FY2027 guidance above forecasts; everything else is macro continuation, routine buybacks or an approval that was likely expected.

The IFX.DE buy has filled (6 at 50.90) and the catalyst is intact, so I hold; no new name-specific catalyst to justify a buy.

The trader bought 6 Infineon shares at the open. The fill was 50.90 euros at 09:15 Frankfurt time. Commission was 2.50 euros, with no FX or tax. The trade is a 10-day bet on that guidance. The reasons: JP Morgan put a Buy rating on it today, and the strong guidance for next year still stands. Infineon closed at 52.12, up from 49.05 yesterday. That is now 2.4 percent above our entry.
